done_when: When forge next runs, it checks at most once a day (cached in the shared Git directory) for the newest Forge release on GitHub and, if it is newer than forge.toml's pin, lists one line: 'Forge vX is out (you pin vY): forge upgrade vX'. It never upgrades by itself; with no network or a failed check it shows nothing and does not slow forge next by more than a few seconds. The skill tells the agent to offer the upgrade to the owner. New and existing repos: every repo on this release sees it. One command-level test: a stubbed newer release shows the line, a failed check shows none, and a second run the same day makes no request.
why: Client repos never learn that a newer Forge release exists, so they stay on old releases and miss every speedup and fix, which only take effect once installed
